name: gosec-2eb4727e-blind30-ots
instr:
# A Go static security scanner gone wrong: 29 undocumented edits, without a test suite

The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. A command-line tool that inspects Go source for security problems, and the library underneath it, now get a great many things wrong. Nothing about the code being inspected changed and nothing about how the tool is invoked changed; inspections that used to come back correctly now come back wrong, and in two places the tool dies outright. What follows is everything noticed from the outside.

Starting with plain invocation. Launching the tool with no paths to inspect at all finishes with a success status, where it used to complain and finish in failure. In the other direction, inspecting code in which nothing at all is found and nothing goes wrong still finishes in failure, and that failure comes back whether or not the switch that asks the tool never to fail is supplied. Handing the tool a document of settings has also stopped doing anything: the values in it are silently dropped, so per-check options and exclusions behave exactly as if an empty document had been supplied.

The biggest visible loss is findings. Code that calls a function through a package-qualified name, which covers nearly every dangerous library call the tool knows about, comes back with nothing flagged. Two further observations point the same way. A file's declared dependencies on other packages are only registered when a package is brought in purely for its side
